prompt.context: Our client is an Eastern U.S. railroad that is required to implement a new technology mandated by the government. The new technology involves installing signal readers at various points along the tracks to communicate train locations and improve safety measures over the next 12 months. They have exceeded their budget on the first 3 installments and have asked us to help them solve the problem.
prompt.question: Why has the client exceeded its budget on the first 3 installments, and what should they do to get the remaining 10 installments back on track?

clarifying_info.q: What is the total budget for the project?
Do we know how far over budget they are?
clarifying_info.a: It varies by installment but they have been over by an average of 15%.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a reason why costs have increased?
clarifying_info.a: The client is unsure and has asked us to help them figure out the cause of increases.

clarifying_info.q: How many more installments do they have?
What is the process to install the new technology?
clarifying_info.a: For each location, the installation team travels to the site daily, works 8AM-5PM, Monday-Friday. They are each assigned a task once they arrive and have the tools to get started.

clarifying_info.q: Has the same team done each of the installations?
clarifying_info.a: It's a core team of installers for each region who travel to various sites. They are the only ones with this type of experience in the regional areas.

exhibits.title: Budget vs. Actual Cost Breakdown
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing budgeted costs versus actual costs, broken down into three cost categories: Materials, Labor, and Miscellaneous.
exhibits.data: Two bars (Budget and Actual) scaled up to approximately $120-$140. The Actual bar is visibly higher than the Budget bar, with Labor appearing as the largest segment and showing the greatest variance.

exhibits.title: Observed Daily Activity
exhibits.shows: A table of average time spent per worker on each observed daily activity during a field study.
exhibits.data: Arrival and daily set up: 20 mins; Gather materials: 20 mins; Team meeting: 30 mins; Signal installation: 5 hours; Breaks (smoking, bathroom): 40 mins; Lunch: 1 hour; Quitting early*: 40 mins; Waiting for new task: 30 mins. *Sometimes workers don't start a new task if it's nearly the end of the day.

framework: Labor costs: wages, overtime, union involvement, minimum wage changes
Labor efficiency: number of people required per task, composition of skilled vs. unskilled workers
Materials costs: cost of inputs, transportation of materials, development/infrastructure costs, inventory control
External factors: competitors experiencing the same issues, weather interference causing longer project times, supplier issues, technology failures

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what is the primary driver of cost overruns?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that Labor is the largest cost category and shows the greatest variance between budget and actual. Materials and Miscellaneous appear relatively in line. The focus of analysis should therefore shift to understanding and reducing labor costs.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 2, identify which activities are non-value add and calculate the total non-value add time per worker per day.
questions.guidance: Candidate should distinguish policy-compliant activities (2x10-min breaks, 1-hour unpaid lunch, mandatory team meetings) from eliminable waste. Non-value add activities to eliminate: Quitting Early (40 mins), half of breaks (20 mins), Waiting for new task (30 mins), and a 75% reduction in Arrival & Gathering Materials (30 mins of the combined 40 mins). Total eliminable time = 40 + 20 + 30 + 30 = 120 minutes = 2 hours.

math.setup: 8-hour workday (8AM-5PM). Identify non-value add time that can be eliminated based on company policy and operational improvements.
steps: Excessive breaks beyond policy: 40 mins total breaks - 20 mins policy (2x10 min) = 20 mins eliminable
Waiting for new task: 30 mins (fully eliminable)
Arrival & gathering materials: 20 + 20 = 40 mins total; can be reduced by 75% = 30 mins eliminable
Total eliminable non-value add time: 40 + 20 + 30 + 30 = 120 mins = 2 hours
Non-value add as % of day: 120 mins / 480 mins = 25%
math.answer: 2 hours (120 minutes) of non-value add time per worker per day, representing 25% of the workday. Eliminating this yields a 25% reduction in labor costs and a ~33% increase in productive output.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific actions can the client take to eliminate or reduce the non-value add activities identified?

categories.name: Operational Improvements
ideas: Work site management and organization to improve setup time and material gathering
Pre-stage materials at the site the evening before to reduce morning setup
Streamline task communication to reduce quitting-early time (foremen assign next tasks before current ones finish)

categories.name: Training
ideas: Supervisor training to allocate work correctly and minimize wait time between tasks
Policy training and reinforcement so workers understand break and schedule expectations

recommendation: The primary driver of budget overruns is excess labor cost, specifically ~25% of each worker's day is spent on non-value add activities including quitting early, excessive breaks, waiting for task assignments, and slow setup and material gathering.

By implementing operational improvements and training to eliminate these 2 hours of daily waste per worker, the client can achieve a 25% reduction in labor costs and restore the project to within budget for the remaining 10 installments.
risks: Downtime during training may temporarily reduce productivity before improvements take effect
Employee morale and pushback from workers asked to change established routines
Regional teams are the only ones with this installation experience, limiting leverage over workforce behavior
next_steps: Prioritize and schedule operational and training initiatives based on ease of implementation and expected impact
Implement work-site pre-staging and task-assignment protocols immediately as quick wins
Roll out supervisor and policy training before the next installment begins
Track budget-to-actual labor hours per installment to verify improvement
